Develop a circuit for echo cancellation that processes a continuous stream of audio signals. The design utilizes additional memory to store delayed feedback values, enabling the filtering and subtraction operations performed synchronously with the clock.

  input signed [n-1:0] in,
  input signed [m-1:0] fb,
  output reg signed [n-1:0] out, // Changed to 'reg' type to store output
  input clk // Added clk as input
);

parameter m = 3; // number of feedback signals

reg signed [m-1:0] fb_filtered [0:n-1];

integer i; // Declare 'i' as an integer

// Delay line
always @(posedge clk) begin
  for (i = 0; i < n; i = i + 1) begin
    fb_delayed[i] <= {fb_delayed[i][m-2:0], fb}; // Note: Corrected fb array access
  end
end

// Filter
always @(posedge clk) begin
  for (i = 0; i < n; i = i + 1) begin
    fb_filtered[i] <= (fb_delayed[i][0] + fb_delayed[i][1] + fb_delayed[i][2]) / 3;
  end
end

// Subtraction

  for (i = 0; i < n; i = i + 1) begin
    out[i] <= in[i] - fb_filtered[i];
  end
end

Instruction: This module is a 10-state finite state machine that acts as a modulo-10 counter, advancing one state per clock. It has an asynchronous active-high reset (rst) and a clock (clk), and produces an 8-bit registered output Q. A 4-bit state register cycles s0 through s9 on each clk rising edge and returns to s0 on a rst rising edge. A combinational decoder maps states to Q values 0–7, then 9 and 10, skipping 8.
Response:
module D2_C1(
input wire rst,
input wire clk,
output reg [7:0] Q
);
parameter [3:0]
  s0 = 0,
  s1 = 1,
  s2 = 2,
  s3 = 3,
  s4 = 4,
  s5 = 5,
  s6 = 6,
  s7 = 7,
  s8 = 8,
  s9 = 9;
reg [3:0] s;
  always @(posedge rst, posedge clk) begin
    if((rst == 1'b1)) begin
      s <= s0;
    end else begin
      case(s)
      s0 : begin
        s <= s1;
      end
      s1 : begin
        s <= s2;
      end
      s2 : begin
        s <= s3;
      end
      s3 : begin
        s <= s4;
      end
      s4 : begin
        s <= s5;
      end
      s5 : begin
        s <= s6;
      end
      s6 : begin
        s <= s7;
      end
      s7 : begin
        s <= s8;
      end
      s8 : begin
        s <= s9;
      end
      s9 : begin
        s <= s0;
      end
      endcase
    end
  end
  always @(s) begin
    case(s)
    s0 : begin
      Q <= 8'b00000000;
    end
    s1 : begin
      Q <= 8'b00000001;
    end
    s2 : begin
      Q <= 8'b00000010;
    end
    s3 : begin
      Q <= 8'b00000011;
    end
    s4 : begin
      Q <= 8'b00000100;
    end
    s5 : begin
      Q <= 8'b00000101;
    end
    s6 : begin
      Q <= 8'b00000110;
    end
    s7 : begin
      Q <= 8'b00000111;
    end
    s8 : begin
      Q <= 8'b00001001;
    end
    s9 : begin
      Q <= 8'b00001010;
    end
    endcase
  end
// rst = 0.5Mhz, clk=10Mhz
endmodule

Instruction: The module implements a turn-signal LED animation driver. Inputs are clock `clk`, active-high reset, and enable `en`; output is 3-bit `led_out`. A six-state finite state machine cycles through LED patterns 000, 100, 110, 111, 011, 001, advancing every 6,250,000 clock cycles via an internal counter. Reset or `en` low clears the state and turns all LEDs off. After the last state it returns to the first, creating a repeating sweep with an off pause.

This module implements a 544-bit rotating shift register that outputs an 8-bit slice. Its ports are a clock, an active-high asynchronous reset, a 544-bit input load value, and an 8-bit output. On reset, the internal 544-bit register loads the input value. Otherwise, each rising clock edge rotates the register right by 8 bits. The output reflects the register’s most-significant 8 bits.

This module converts a 4-bit BCD digit into a 7-bit seven-segment display pattern. It has inputs clk and bcd[3:0], plus a registered 7-bit output segment7. A case statement maps BCD values 0–9 to their segment codes, while invalid values (10–15) blank the display. The block triggers on the rising edge of clk or any change on bcd, so it acts asynchronously rather than as a purely clocked register.

This module implements a positive-edge-triggered D flip-flop with an asynchronous active-high reset. Its inputs are a data input, a clock, and a reset; its output is the registered value. When reset is asserted, the output is cleared to zero immediately, regardless of the clock. Otherwise, on each rising clock edge, the output captures and stores the current data input. Reset therefore has priority over normal data loading.

module dff(
input wire d,
input wire clk,
input wire reset,
output reg q
);
  always @(posedge clk, posedge reset) begin
    if((reset == 1'b1)) begin
      q <= 1'b0;
    end else begin
      q <= d;
    end
  end
endmodule

Instruction: This module is a forwarding and hazard-control unit for a pipelined processor. Its inputs are the ID-stage source registers, the ID/EXE destination and control signals, and the EXE/MEM destination and write-enable; its outputs are pipeline enable/bubble signals and two ALU forwarding selects. It detects a load-use hazard when the ID/EXE stage is a memory access writing a register that matches either ID source register, stalling the PC, IF/ID, and ID/EXE stages and inserting a bubble; otherwise it enables those stages. For each source operand it compares against the ID/EXE and EXE/MEM destinations with write-enable, selecting forward-from-ID/EXE, forward-from-EXE/MEM, or no forwarding.

This module is a 4-bit to 8-bit seven-segment display decoder that converts a hexadecimal digit into active-low segment drive signals. It has a 4-bit input `enabler_input` and an 8-bit registered output `enabler_output`. A combinational always block uses a case statement to map inputs 0000 through 1001 to the segment patterns for digits 0–9. Any other input falls to a default pattern that displays a “u” symbol.

Design a synchronous circuit that outputs a value based on the state of the inputs R, C, and D. When the clock signal C has a rising edge, if R is LOW, the output Q is set to LOW. If R is HIGH, the output Q retains its current value unless it is LOW and D is HIGH, in which case Q takes the value of D; otherwise, Q remains unchanged. This effectively allows the module to select between a reset operation and a conditional updating mechanism informed by the inputs.

    finish : begin
      etat_futur <= init;
    end
    endcase

    init : begin
      start <= 1'b0;
    end
    calcul : begin
      start <= 1'b0;
